content2.content: The `GestureDetector` widget is the workhorse of interaction in Flutter. It doesn't have a visual representation but detects gestures made on its child.

content4.content: Wrap any widget with `GestureDetector` to make it interactive.

content5.content:
GestureDetector(
  onTap: () => print('Tap'),
  onLongPress: () => print('Long Press'),
  onHorizontalDragEnd: (details) => print('Swiped'),
  child: Container(padding: EdgeInsets.all(20), child: Text('Touch Me')),
)

content7.content: You can control how the detector behaves during hit testing using the `behavior` property (e.g., `HitTestBehavior.opaque`).

content9.content: It is the most flexible way to handle gestures, supporting everything from simple taps to complex custom gestures.
